summary: The note reviews several emergency responses to power and internet outages in 2023-2024 and argues that fast reaction, interagency coordination, technology, community volunteers and private-sector help determine how well a community recovers. Case examples include Ashton, Brenford, Marley, Elmsfield and Crestview. It concludes that adaptable response plans built on these elements are the key to effective crisis management.
one_line: Case studies from Ashton, Brenford, Marley, Elmsfield and Crestview show how speed, collaboration, technology, community and business involvement improve outage emergency response.
key_facts: A storm hit the town of Ashton shortly after midnight on September 5, 2023, causing power and internet outages.
Mayor Teresa Watkins launched Ashton's emergency response plan within an hour of the first outage report.
Dr. Josephine Marks, director of the Department of Crisis Resource Management at Ashton University, said "The golden hours following any disaster are crucial."
On October 19, 2023, a cyber-attack crippled the electrical grid in the city of Brenford, leaving the metropolitan area without power.
Coordinator Alex Torres led a multi-agency task force in Brenford, which became known as the Brenford Protocol.
The Brenford Protocol united municipal services, cybersecurity firms, the National Guard and volunteer organizations, and restored power to critical infrastructure within 48 hours.
On November 11, 2023, the rural township of Marley suffered a catastrophic internet outage.
Marley emergency operations manager Adrian Perez used a cloud-based logistics platform for real-time resource tracking and communication between on-ground teams and remote technical experts.
Perez said "Modern disasters require modern solutions."

In Elmsfield, community organizer Susan McAllister set up a volunteer hub where locals registered skills and availability, including electricians, IT professionals and retired nurses, after a service outage on December 15, 2023.
On January 8, 2024, heavy snowfall disrupted services and closed roads in Crestview.
Jonathan Harlow's company, QuickTransit Logistics, offered its fleet of all-terrain vehicles to support emergency responders in Crestview.
The note concludes that speed, cooperation, technology integration, community involvement and private-sector inclusion are the foundations of effective response.
